ai.title: Release 1.0.469
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.469 in npm-app/release/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The software just got a new internal version number (1.0.469), which is like a behind-the-scenes label that helps keep track of what changes are included. This version bundles a collection of smaller updates that mostly improve how the assistant works internally. Key improvements include better handling of long conversations by trimming unnecessary messages, more accurate tracking of how much each helper agent costs to run, and a smoother process for running automated coding evaluations. There are also some security and login-related updates that make account management more reliable, and a new way to confirm actions using a custom dialog box instead of the standard browser popup. If you use the assistant, you might notice slightly more stable behavior during long coding sessions and cleaner handling of agent-driven tasks, but most of these changes are not directly visible to you.

ai.title: Clarify parallel execution in spawnagents tool description
ai.summary: Updated the `spawn_agents` tool description in `common/src/tools/params/tool/spawn-agents.ts` to explicitly state that spawned agents run in parallel and independently. The new text instructs users to invoke `spawn_agents` with a single agent per call if sequential execution is required. This change affects the core tool parameters definition, ensuring the LLM understands the concurrency model.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to spawn multiple helper agents at once, those agents now clearly run side-by-side rather than one after another. If you intended for them to execute strictly in order, you must now issue a single spawn_agents request per agent and wait for one to finish before starting the next. The wording you see in the assistant's tool guidance is the only thing that changed, so anything depending on the previous text now reflects this parallel and independent execution model.

ai.title: scripts/run-tests-summary replaces inline test hooks
ai.summary: New `scripts/run-tests-summary` script replaces inline `find | xargs | grep` commands in `codebuff.json` file-change hooks. Script aggregates Bun test output into single success line while preserving verbose failure logs. Affects `backend`, `npm-app`, and `common` unit test hooks.

eli5.text: When a developer saves a test file, the system now runs all unit tests across the backend, npm-app, and common packages using a single consolidated step instead of searching and running each test file individually inline. If every test passes, you see one clear success line; if any test fails, you still get the full detailed output so problems can be debugged. The new runner also handles the case where a package has no test files, reporting zero tests rather than erroring out. This is live today for internal developers working in those three package areas.

ai.title: Base2 prompting tweaks
ai.summary: Base2 agent prompts updated to enforce conciseness and clarify editor spawning. `base2-factory.ts` adds a rule to suppress final summaries unless a single sentence is needed. `editor.ts` allows direct spawning for easy tasks without prior scouting or planning, and mandates specific content (answer, changes, checks) in `set_output` summaries.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do something, it will now keep its replies shorter and skip long wrap-up summaries unless a quick one-liner is needed. It can also jump straight into small tasks without first scouting around or making a plan, and when it reports back on a task, it now includes a quick answer, a note on what changed, and a check that things look right.

ai.title: Remove applyAndRevertChangesSequentially from evals scaffolding
ai.summary: Deleted `applyAndRevertChangesSequentially` helper and its `applyAndRevertChanges` import from `evals/scaffolding.ts`. The function implemented a promise queue to serialize file change operations, which is no longer required. Scope limited to internal evals tooling.

eli5.text: The behind-the-scenes testing system for the assistant quietly dropped an old helper that coordinated file changes in a strict order. If you were watching the internal test scaffolding, that coordination logic is simply gone. Nothing you can see or do is changed by this.

ai.title: Move cache control into convertCbToModelMessages
ai.summary: Cache control injection moved from `getMessagesSubset` to `convertCbToModelMessages` via new `includeCacheControl` flag on `promptAiSdkStream`, `promptAiSdk`, `promptAiSdkStructured`, and `getAgentStreamFromTemplate`. `run-agent-step.ts` now passes `supportsCacheControl(model)` at call time instead of post-hoc message mutation. `withCacheControl` uses `deepCopy` and a new `withoutCacheControl` strips stale `anthropic`/`openrouter` cache entries. `CodebuffMessage` schemas in `common/src/types/messages/codebuff-message.ts` gained shared `auxiliaryDataSchema` for `providerOptions`, `timeToLive`, `keepDuringTruncation`.

eli5.text: The assistant now receives an early heads-up about which conversations are allowed to use cached context before it starts processing each step, rather than marking them as cacheable only after the messages were already assembled. This means the caching decision is made at prompt-send time based on whether the model supports it, and stale caching tags are copied out instead of mutating the original message history in place. For you as an end user there is no visible difference today, since the behavior (what gets cached and when) has not changed; the change only reorganizes the internal plumbing so the cache-control instructions travel with the request from the start rather than being bolted onto the message list afterward. This is a behind-the-scenes refactor in the backend that leaves the

ai.title: Remove debug and file-resolver utilities, clean logger imports
ai.summary: Deleted `backend/src/util/debug.ts` and `backend/src/util/file-resolver.ts` to remove unused filesystem-dependent helpers. `backend/src/util/logger.ts` dropped an unused `AsyncLocalStorage` import from `async_hooks`. Internal cleanup; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: The team removed some behind-the-scenes debugging tools from the system that were used during development but aren't needed now. These tools wrote log files to the server's filesystem and resolved file paths for prompts, but since the system doesn't rely on them anymore, they were deleted entirely. The logging system also had some leftover code removed that wasn't being used. Nothing you see or do in the application changes - this is purely internal cleanup. If you happened to look at the server's file structure, you'd notice these debugging files are simply gone.

ai.title: Fix import path in common/src/util/object.ts
ai.summary: Corrected relative import path for JSONValue type in `common/src/util/object.ts`. Replaced `src/types/json` with `../types/json` to resolve typecheck errors. Affects shared core utilities only.

eli5.text: Some shared code that many parts of the product rely on had a broken reference to a helper tool it needed. The system was looking for that helper in the wrong place, which caused it to stop loading correctly. Engineers corrected the reference so it points to the right location, and since then everything that depends on those shared utilities works again. If you were to look at the affected tool now, it would load without the error message that used to appear.

ai.title: Remove trace and fileStates from eval process console output
ai.summary: Strips `trace` and `eval_commit.fileStates` from the `Final result` log in `evals/git-evals/run-single-eval-process.ts`. The full `result` object remains available via `process.send` for IPC consumers. This reduces console noise during eval execution.

eli5.text: When the system runs an evaluation in the background and prints the final result to the console, it no longer includes two pieces of detailed internal information: a step-by-step history of what happened and a list of files that were changed. However, that full information is still sent to other programs listening in, so nothing important is lost. You would notice the console output looking cleaner during eval runs, with less clutter from very technical details.

ai.title: Remove unused mock from agent-validation.test.ts
ai.summary: Removed unused mockModule for @codebuff/backend/util/file-resolver in common/src/__tests__/agent-validation.test.ts. Cleanup of dead test setup code. Scope limited to test file. No behavior change.

eli5.text: A leftover instruction that told the automated testing system how to fake a helper tool was deleted from one of the validation test files. This is purely behind-the-scenes cleanup: nothing you see, run, or rely on changes behavior. Developers will notice the test file is shorter and its setup section is simpler. It's live now, but only affects how tests are written, not what they check.

When an evaluation finishes, it no longer prints the full step-by-step trace or file state snapshots of intermediate commits, making the logs cleaner for anyone reviewing them. This is internal housekeeping with no visible effect on end users today; you wouldn't notice any difference in functionality, just shorter, less cluttered logs for developers who inspect them.

ai.title: Editor prompt bans code comments; scout prompt tightens output
ai.summary: Editor instructions now forbid all code comments unless the user explicitly requests them, replacing the prior 'sparingly' guidance. Scout agent prompt prohibits narrating spawn parameters and bans irrelevant info, end-of-turn summaries, and follow-up questions in responses. base2-factory prompt changed final-summary rule from 'maybe one sentence' to a strict single completion sentence. ModelName type in agent-definition.ts adds openai/gpt-5-chat alongside existing gpt-5 variants.

ai.title: Increase MAXAGENTSTEPSDEFAULT to 40
ai.summary: The default `MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT` constant in `common/src/constants/agents.ts` increased from 25 to 40. This adjustment compensates for the context-pruner consuming half of the available steps, ensuring sufficient headroom for agent execution. This change affects the core shared configuration used by the agent loop.

eli5.text: When you give the assistant a task, it works through it in a series of small steps. That step limit was raised from 25 to 40, so the assistant can now take longer before it has to stop. You’d notice this if you’ve ever hit a point where the assistant says it ran out of steps before finishing, that ceiling is now higher.

ai.title: Base2 agent config fixes
ai.summary: Base2 factory adds add_message to toolNames and updates step-limit prompt to require plain text. Editor stepLimit increased from 15 to 20. Covers .agents/base2/base2-factory.ts and .agents/base2/editor.ts.

eli5.text: The automated coding assistant can now leave itself reminder notes while working on a task, and the editor helper is allowed to keep working five steps longer before stopping. If you were watching, you'd see the helper try a bit harder to finish before handing control back, and occasionally use a new tool to write itself a quick message mid-flow. These are small behind-the-scenes adjustments to how long the helper works and what tools it can use.

ai.title: Fix setmessages filter in codebuff eval runner
ai.summary: CodebuffRunner now filters set_messages tool calls by checking event.toolName instead of event.toolCallId. Previous logic failed to match the tool name, causing set_messages calls to incorrectly enter the toolCalls array. Scope limited to evals/git-evals/runners/codebuff.ts. Correct property access ensures internal message-setting calls are properly excluded from eval traces.

eli5.text: When the system records what the assistant does during an evaluation, it was accidentally keeping internal bookkeeping notes in the same list as real actions. It now correctly ignores those internal notes so the recorded trace only shows actual tool usage. You wouldn't see anything different unless you're reviewing the raw evaluation logs, where those stray internal notes will no longer appear.

ai.title: Remove ungenerated evals from git-evals specs
ai.summary: Deleted all entries with spec 'Failed to generate specification due to error' from `evals/git-evals/eval-plane.json` and `evals/git-evals/eval-saleor.json`. These entries contained broken or incomplete file states from failed generation runs. Removing them cleans up the eval dataset by excluding invalid or non-runnable test cases.

eli5.text: The system cleaned up its internal test dataset by removing entries that were created by failed generation attempts. If you looked at the test cases used to train the assistant, you would see that broken or incomplete test scenarios were stripped out, leaving behind only valid and runnable examples. This affects the quality of the data the assistant learns from, but you wouldn't notice it directly in your conversations.

ai.title: Cost aggregation integration test filename and assertions fixed
ai.summary: `backend/src/__tests__/cost-aggregation.integration.test.ts` renamed from `cost-aggregation-integration.test.ts`, imports trimmed, `stepsRemaining` pinned to 10. Stabilizes `mainPrompt` cost flow assertions, replaces range checks with `toEqual(73)` / `toEqual(50)`. Backend test-only scope, no runtime surfaces.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team fixed some internal tests that check how the assistant tracks the cost of running a coding task. These tests now expect specific, exact credit totals instead of a rough range, and they lock in a fixed number of steps so the numbers stay predictable. If you looked at this area, you'd only see tidier test files and tighter checks, no change to how the assistant actually works for you today.

ai.title: GPT-5 Quick Thinker adds publisher field, experimental mode uses base2
ai.summary: The `gpt5-thinker` agent definition now imports and sets `publisher` from `../constants`, aligning it with the standard agent template. In `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, the `experimental` cost mode maps to the literal string `'base2'` instead of `AgentTemplateTypes.base_experimental`. Scope covers `.agents/deep-thinking/gpt5-thinker.ts` and `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. The `base2` value is a raw string, not an enum member.

eli5.text: The GPT-5 Quick Thinker agent now shows who published it and uses a new internal configuration named 'base2' when running in experimental mode. You would notice this by seeing the publisher attribution on the agent and, if you use experimental settings, the system switching to a different prompting style labeled 'base2' instead of the previous type. This is an internal change for developers and does not affect general users, but it is live now in the agent definition and backend configuration.

ai.title: Cache control moved to last content block
ai.summary: Refactored `withCacheControl` and `withoutCacheControl` in `common/src/util/messages.ts` to operate on generic objects with `providerOptions` instead of `CodebuffMessage`. `convertCbToModelMessages` now applies cache control to the final content block of the last message, rather than the entire message object. This ensures Anthropic/OpenRouter ephemeral caching targets the correct granularity.

eli5.text: The assistant's memory of recent conversations now expires from the right spot instead of the whole message. When the system saves a cached copy of your chat to speed up future replies, it attaches that cache marker to the very last piece of content (the closing words) rather than the entire message block. If you were inspecting how those cached replies are stored, you'd see the cache label sitting on the final line of text instead of wrapping the full message.

ai.title: Add TEST! log to websocket prompt handler
ai.summary: Added a duplicate logger.info call with 'TEST!' prefix in backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts. This change introduces redundant logging for user prompts within the onPrompt handler. Scope limited to backend websocket actions. No functional behavior change; purely diagnostic logging addition.

eli5.text: When you type a prompt to the assistant in a chat session, the system now writes that same prompt to its internal log file a second time, tagging the duplicate line with "TEST!" so engineers can spot it more easily during debugging. Only backend server logs are affected; your chat experience stays exactly the same, and no new features are exposed to users today.

ai.title: Fix typecheck in common/src/util/messages.ts
ai.summary: Corrected import path for ProviderMetadata in common/src/util/messages.ts. Replaced 'src/...' with relative '../types/...' to resolve typecheck failure. Scope limited to Shared/Core.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal messaging tool had a small typo-like bug: it was looking for a piece of shared information at the wrong address, so the system that checks everything is typed correctly (a 'typecheck') was failing. Developers fixed the address on one line, pointing it back to where that information actually lives. For you as a user, nothing changes in how the assistant behaves today this was background housekeeping to keep the code valid and stable. You would notice no difference unless you build the software from source yourself.

ai.title: Replace custom object utils with lodash
ai.summary: Replaced custom `hasKey` and `deepEqual` utilities in `common/src/util/object.ts` with `lodash`'s `has` and `isEqual`. This refactoring reduces code duplication by leveraging existing dependencies. The change affects `common/src/util/messages.ts` where these utilities are used for cache control and message aggregation logic.

eli5.text: The program no longer relies on its own hand-written helpers to check if something exists in a set of options or to tell whether two sets of options are the same when filtering out cached-response markers and grouping similar messages together. Those checks now use a widely-used, pre-existing library instead, which trims away roughly an hour's worth of custom code without altering what the program does. If you look at this work, it is already in the released software, and to a user nothing should appear different except a small amount of cleaner internal logic.

ai.title: CodebuffRunner creates client per request
ai.summary: CodebuffRunner now instantiates a new CodebuffClient for every run instead of caching a single instance. This change removes the persistent client state, ensuring fresh connections and error handling contexts per execution. The modification applies to the evals/git-evals/runners/codebuff.ts file. Clients are explicitly closed via client.closeConnection() after each run completes.

eli5.text: When the tool finishes running an assistant session for evaluation, it now starts a completely fresh connection each time instead of reusing the same one from a previous run. The old behavior kept a single shared connection around, but now every run gets its own clean connection that is explicitly closed when the run ends. If you were watching these evaluation runs, you might notice slightly more setup work at the beginning of each run and a cleaner teardown at the end, with no leftover connection state carrying over between runs.

ai.title: Fix DEFAULTBACKENDURL typo in SDK
ai.summary: Corrects DEFAULT_BACKEND_URL from 'manidoce-backend.onrender.com' to 'manicode-backend.onrender.com' in sdk/src/constants.ts. The previous value contained a character swap in the hostname. This ensures the SDK defaults to the correct production backend endpoint.

eli5.text: A small number of people using the developer kit that lets other tools talk to the service will now be connected to the right server by default. Previously, a misspelled web address quietly pointed them to a non-working site; now it points to the correct one. You wouldn't see any visible change unless you were setting up the developer kit yourself, in which case it would simply succeed where it previously failed.

ai.title: Eval runner logs invalid tool errors instead of throwing
ai.summary: Eval runner `codebuff.ts` logs error events via `console.log` instead of throwing, preventing crash on invalid tool call. `xml-stream-parser.ts` increases invalid JSON error message content truncation limit from 50 to 200 chars. `messages.ts` and `run-git-evals.ts` replace custom `deepCopy` with `lodash` `cloneDeep` to preserve types/functions. `object.ts` removes unused `deepCopy` export.

eli5.text: When the evaluation system that tests the assistant encounters a problem with a tool call, it now prints the error to the screen instead of stopping the entire run. This means automated test runs are more resilient and won't crash just because one step had an issue. You would notice the run continuing past errors instead of halting, with error details appearing in the output log. This is live today for anyone running git-based automated tests.

ai.title: changes.ts error logging uses errorToObject
ai.summary: Refactored error logging in `applyChanges` within `npm-app/src/utils/changes.ts` to use `errorToObject` from `@codebuff/common/util/object`. This ensures error objects are serialized correctly in console output during patch application failures. Scope limited to `npm-app` utility module. Internal change; no user-facing behavior or API surface modifications.

eli5.text: When the system tries to apply a set of edits to files and something goes wrong, it used to print a messy, incomplete description of the error. Now it prints a clean, complete version of that error message instead. This only affects the internal tools the team uses to make changes to projects, so you won't see any difference in the software you use day to day. It's like switching from a scribbled note to a properly formatted report when something fails behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add posthog-node dependency to common package
ai.summary: Added 'posthog-node' (^5.8.0) to dependencies in common/package.json. This integrates server-side analytics capabilities into the shared core module. Scope limited to common package manifest.

eli5.text: The shared core module now includes a server-side analytics tool, so teams building on it can quietly start tracking how features are used on the backend. Only the core module's package list was updated; no new features are visible yet to anyone using it. This is a behind-the-scenes dependency addition, live today in the core package.

ai.title: Stream single agent output with labeled dividers
ai.summary: Refactored agent spawning to stream outputs for any single child agent, removing hardcoded allowlists. `executeAgent` now accepts `isOnlyChild` flag to inject labeled start/end dividers into the stream. `runProgrammaticStep` emits tool calls to client immediately. Files: `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`, `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-inline.ts`, `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts`, `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agents.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask an assistant to break a big job into separate steps and then run only one of those steps alone, the system now wraps that step's output with clear labeled headers, so you can see exactly where that single step begins and ends as it streams back to you. Previously this only happened for a couple of specific assistant types that were hard-coded into a list; now it happens for any single step you run this way. If you triggered one-step-off-a-multi-step-plan runs today, you'll notice the start/end labels around the streamed output that weren't there before.

ai.title: Patch failures returned as tool result, not thrown
ai.summary: Patch application errors in `applyChanges` now return `false` as a `patchFailed` array item instead of throwing. `handleUpdateFile` and `changeFile` consume this array to append 'Failed to write to ${file}; the patch failed to apply' to the tool result string. This prevents unhandled exceptions from crashing the agent loop when a diff context mismatch occurs. Covers `npm-app` tool handlers and `sdk` change-file tool.

eli5.text: When a code-editing tool tries to apply a patch to a file, it no longer throws a hard error and crashes if the patch cannot be applied due to a context mismatch; instead, it logs the failure and continues. You'll now see a message like 'Failed to write to <file>; the patch failed to apply' added to the tool result, rather than the entire editing process stopping. This affects the agent loop handling file updates via the SDK and npm-app tools.
